glossary.astrology.keyword.self_awarenes: Observe choices and feelings, then revise through experience.

Self-awareness means observing choices, feelings, and habits, then revising an interpretation through experience. A natal chart can suggest reflective questions, while actual behavior remains grounded in life circumstances rather than a fixed chart identity.
glossary.astrology.keyword.curiosity.sho: Explore another perspective through questions and practice.
glossary.astrology.keyword.curiosity.lon: Curiosity means exploring different perspectives through questions, comparison, and practice. Turn a chart theme into an observable question, examine it through concrete experience, and allow new information to change an earlier view.
glossary.astrology.keyword.cooperation.s: Clarify needs and find an arrangement both people can revise.
glossary.astrology.keyword.cooperation.l: Cooperation means clarifying each person’s needs and finding an arrangement both can revise. Chart themes may help frame questions, while roles, communication, and commitments are agreed by the people involved.

glossary.hexagram.1.short: The doubled heaven image emphasizes initiative that changes with its stage of development.
glossary.hexagram.1.long: The doubled heaven image emphasizes initiative that changes with its stage of development. Preparation, visible responsibility and restraint are different uses of strength. Read the dragon sequence as a question about readiness, rather than permission to keep expanding every undertaking.
glossary.hexagram.2.short: The doubled earth image emphasizes carrying and sustaining an arrangement.
glossary.hexagram.2.long: The doubled earth image emphasizes carrying and sustaining an arrangement. Receptivity differs from surrendering judgment. Establish the direction you are agreeing to support, then make that support dependable through repeated actions rather than competing to set every part of the agenda.
glossary.hexagram.3.short: Thunder beneath water places an impulse to begin under difficult conditions.
glossary.hexagram.3.long: Thunder beneath water places an impulse to begin under difficult conditions. The issue is organizing an early undertaking, rather than proving courage through solitary effort. Find people who can share the preparation and establish the working arrangement before asking the whole project to move at once.
glossary.hexagram.4.short: Water beneath the mountain frames uncertainty as a learning situation.
glossary.hexagram.4.long: Water beneath the mountain frames uncertainty as a learning situation. A useful teaching relationship needs an answerable question and willingness to practise. Repeating the request without using the instruction may add little. Clarify what you are trying to learn and which exercise would show whether the explanation helped.
glossary.hexagram.5.short: Water above heaven places difficulty ahead of an active force.
glossary.hexagram.5.long: Water above heaven places difficulty ahead of an active force. Waiting here has a purpose: preserve usable resources while the missing condition develops. It differs from postponing everything indefinitely. Identify what you are actually waiting for and continue the preparation that does not require crossing the present obstacle.
glossary.hexagram.6.short: Heaven and water move in different ways, providing an image of diverging aims.
glossary.hexagram.6.long: Heaven and water move in different ways, providing an image of diverging aims. The practical concern is how a disagreement escalates and where it can be stopped. Return to an agreement the participants can fulfil, and seek fair mediation where useful, rather than making victory the only acceptable ending.
glossary.hexagram.7.short: Water held within earth presents collective capacity that needs organization.
glossary.hexagram.7.long: Water held within earth presents collective capacity that needs organization. Having many participants does not establish a coordinated effort. The reading asks about a capable organizer, shared rules and clear instructions. Agree on responsibilities and handover so that competing directions do not consume the group’s available energy.
glossary.hexagram.8.short: Water resting on earth gives an image of connection.
glossary.hexagram.8.long: Water resting on earth gives an image of connection. The issue is choosing a group or partner through willingness and reliability, rather than proximity alone. Establish the shared purpose and ask how each person wants to participate. A sound association leaves room for a voluntary response instead of demanding immediate allegiance.
glossary.hexagram.9.term: The Taming Power of the Small
glossary.hexagram.9.short: Wind above heaven suggests a limited influence shaping a stronger impulse.
glossary.hexagram.9.long: Wind above heaven suggests a limited influence shaping a stronger impulse. Small adjustments can collect useful capacity before a larger undertaking is ready. This differs from the Great Taming’s more substantial reserve. Improve a detail or a conversation, and check the supporting arrangement before treating modest progress as permission to expand.
glossary.hexagram.10.short: Heaven above the lake presents a crossing of sensitive boundaries.
glossary.hexagram.10.long: Heaven above the lake presents a crossing of sensitive boundaries. Careful conduct concerns the way you proceed, not a requirement to retreat from every encounter. Check the procedure, your authority to act and the other person’s needs. A plain, well-prepared approach can preserve dignity without relying on display or force.
glossary.hexagram.11.short: Earth above heaven represents an exchange between complementary movements.
glossary.hexagram.11.long: Earth above heaven represents an exchange between complementary movements. The point is circulation and access, rather than an everlasting favourable condition. Use a period of communication to establish clear responsibilities and ways to maintain contact. A workable routine helps the relationship remain usable when the initial ease is no longer new.
glossary.hexagram.12.short: Heaven above earth presents movements that do not readily meet.
glossary.hexagram.12.long: Heaven above earth presents movements that do not readily meet. Unlike Peace, the emphasis is on blocked exchange and preserving what remains workable. Do not count an unanswered request as an agreement. Protect essential resources and look for a limited point of contact through which communication can begin again.
glossary.hexagram.13.short: Fire beneath heaven emphasizes a purpose that can be recognized across personal circles.
glossary.hexagram.13.long: Fire beneath heaven emphasizes a purpose that can be recognized across personal circles. Shared understanding is different from loyalty only to familiar people. State the task in terms newcomers can use, and make participation accessible. This helps a group build common ground without requiring everyone to share the same background or preferences.
glossary.hexagram.14.short: Fire above heaven brings resources into visibility.
glossary.hexagram.14.long: Fire above heaven brings resources into visibility. Unlike the Great Taming’s preparation of reserves, this reading asks how an existing capacity is used and shared. Make contribution and responsibility clear. The usefulness of a resource depends on access and stewardship, rather than on displaying how much one person possesses.
glossary.hexagram.15.short: The mountain within earth suggests real substance expressed without occupying the highest visible place.
glossary.hexagram.15.long: The mountain within earth suggests real substance expressed without occupying the highest visible place. Modesty does not require denying a contribution. Describe what you completed plainly while acknowledging what others supplied. This keeps the scale of the account close to the work and allows competence to remain visible without turning it into a contest for attention.
glossary.hexagram.16.short: Thunder emerging above earth suggests energy that can mobilize a group.
glossary.hexagram.16.long: Thunder emerging above earth suggests energy that can mobilize a group. Enthusiasm becomes useful when preparation lets others join the movement. Check the people, materials and sequence needed before relying on the atmosphere itself. If excitement has displaced attention to a constraint, return to that condition without dismissing the value of shared motivation.
glossary.hexagram.17.short: Thunder within the lake suggests movement responding to a wider situation.
glossary.hexagram.17.long: Thunder within the lake suggests movement responding to a wider situation. Following differs from accepting every influence unexamined. Identify the purpose you recognize before deciding how to adapt. A change of direction may alter a previous association, so explain the choice and the limits of your participation rather than relying on silent compliance.
glossary.hexagram.18.term: Work on What Has Been Spoiled
glossary.hexagram.18.short: Wind beneath the mountain frames a problem accumulated through neglect or an arrangement left unexamined.
glossary.hexagram.18.long: Wind beneath the mountain frames a problem accumulated through neglect or an arrangement left unexamined. Repair requires attention to causes as well as appearances. Separate an inherited habit from its present effects and from the process that now needs updating. Correct one source of deterioration, then check whether the repair remains effective in ordinary use.
glossary.hexagram.19.short: Earth above the lake suggests approaching and attending to a situation.
glossary.hexagram.19.long: Earth above the lake suggests approaching and attending to a situation. Closeness becomes useful through understanding, not merely supervision. A favourable opening also has limits and needs maintenance. Visit the actual task, listen to the people carrying it and agree how you will remain available after the first approach.
glossary.hexagram.20.short: Wind moving above earth gives a broad view that still needs evidence from practice.
glossary.hexagram.20.long: Wind moving above earth gives a broad view that still needs evidence from practice. Observation includes the example you set, as well as what you notice in others. A limited viewpoint cannot establish the whole arrangement. Compare accounts from different participants and examine your own contribution before deciding what the larger pattern requires.
glossary.hexagram.21.short: Thunder and lightning bring action together with clear discrimination.
glossary.hexagram.21.long: Thunder and lightning bring action together with clear discrimination. The image of an obstruction calls for identifying what prevents connection, not for escalating punishment. Specify the blocked step and choose a correction proportionate to its effect. A clear boundary works better when the relevant facts can be checked and the people affected can understand the response.
glossary.hexagram.22.short: Fire beneath the mountain illuminates a form without replacing its substance.
glossary.hexagram.22.long: Fire beneath the mountain illuminates a form without replacing its substance. Presentation can help people recognize what is being offered, but ornament cannot make an unusable arrangement sound. Check accuracy or function before refining appearance. A simple presentation may fit the occasion better than adding detail that obscures the central purpose.
glossary.hexagram.23.short: The mountain resting above earth directs attention to the support beneath a visible structure.
glossary.hexagram.23.long: The mountain resting above earth directs attention to the support beneath a visible structure. When that support is being stripped away, expansion may add load where capacity is already weakening. Identify the layer that needs protection and preserve essential resources. A smaller workable arrangement can be a more useful response than trying to restore the whole structure immediately.
glossary.hexagram.24.short: Thunder within earth suggests a movement returning before it is fully visible.
glossary.hexagram.24.long: Thunder within earth suggests a movement returning before it is fully visible. A small correction deserves protection rather than an immediate demand for full speed. Resume one practice that can be sustained and notice what helps it continue. This differs from a dramatic restart: the value lies in maintaining the first useful turn back toward a workable path.
glossary.hexagram.25.short: Thunder beneath heaven emphasizes action without contrived motives or unnecessary additions.
glossary.hexagram.25.long: Thunder beneath heaven emphasizes action without contrived motives or unnecessary additions. An unexpected difficulty does not by itself establish personal fault. Separate what belongs to your responsibility from what arose through circumstances, then respond to the effect you can actually address. Honest effort does not require inventing another intervention every time an outcome remains uncertain.
glossary.hexagram.26.term: The Taming Power of the Great
glossary.hexagram.26.short: The mountain above heaven places a strong impulse within a containing structure.
glossary.hexagram.26.long: The mountain above heaven places a strong impulse within a containing structure. The emphasis is on developing capacity and learning when to use it. Restraint is different from keeping a skill unused indefinitely. Check readiness and the means of support, then turn the reserve into a delivery that tests what the preparation has made possible.
glossary.hexagram.27.short: Thunder beneath the mountain gives an image associated with nourishment and the mouth.
glossary.hexagram.27.long: Thunder beneath the mountain gives an image associated with nourishment and the mouth. The question extends beyond food to information, speech and the support you provide. Examine a recurring input that consumes attention without helping the present task. Choose something that meets an actual need, and consider whether what you offer others is equally usable.
glossary.hexagram.28.short: The lake above wood accompanies an image of a beam carrying unusual weight.
glossary.hexagram.28.long: The lake above wood accompanies an image of a beam carrying unusual weight. The issue is load and support before any claim about breakthrough. Reduce nonessential aims and distribute the central responsibility among people able to carry it. Continuing to demonstrate endurance can leave the structure weaker, while a well-supported exception may make a necessary passage workable.
glossary.hexagram.29.short: Repeated water emphasizes difficulty encountered more than once.
glossary.hexagram.29.long: Repeated water emphasizes difficulty encountered more than once. A reliable method can make one short passage usable without promising that every obstacle disappears. Check the foothold for each step and ask for assistance when the same blockage returns. Consistency here concerns staying truthful and attentive within a hard situation, rather than repeating a failed approach simply because it is familiar.
glossary.hexagram.30.short: Repeated fire suggests clarity that depends on something it can attach to and sustain.
glossary.hexagram.30.long: Repeated fire suggests clarity that depends on something it can attach to and sustain. Enthusiasm needs a usable base. Identify the information, tools or people that support the action you want to take. The question is not whether you can shine independently of everything else, but whether your chosen connection can keep the effort clear and manageable.
glossary.hexagram.31.short: The lake above the mountain frames influence through mutual responsiveness.
glossary.hexagram.31.long: The lake above the mountain frames influence through mutual responsiveness. A feeling in one person does not establish the other person’s intention. Unlike Duration’s continuing practice, this reading begins with noticing an exchange. Offer a clear invitation and leave room for a voluntary answer, rather than trying to secure closeness through repeated interpretation of small signs.
glossary.hexagram.32.short: Thunder above wind presents continuity through changing movements.
glossary.hexagram.32.long: Thunder above wind presents continuity through changing movements. Keeping a direction does not require repeating the same method regardless of conditions. Identify the commitment worth maintaining and prepare handover or review when schedules change. Duration becomes practical through renewed follow-through, rather than through insisting that a difficult arrangement must remain untouched to prove loyalty.
glossary.hexagram.33.short: Heaven above the mountain frames a measured withdrawal when engagement no longer fits the conditions.
glossary.hexagram.33.long: Heaven above the mountain frames a measured withdrawal when engagement no longer fits the conditions. Stepping back is different from surrendering every principle. Explain the scope you are leaving, complete the needed handover and preserve distance from an unproductive exchange. This gives a future choice room without requiring you to win the final conversation.
glossary.hexagram.34.short: Thunder above heaven emphasizes increased force that still needs appropriate limits.
glossary.hexagram.34.long: Thunder above heaven emphasizes increased force that still needs appropriate limits. Strength can become an obstacle if it pushes beyond the available route. Check authority, access and support before applying more effort. If movement becomes blocked, change the method rather than treating resistance as a demand to prove that the same force can be made even stronger.
glossary.hexagram.35.short: Fire rising above earth brings progress into visibility.
glossary.hexagram.35.long: Fire rising above earth brings progress into visibility. Recognition becomes useful when it is tied to a contribution people can identify. Explain the part already completed and continue the practices that made it reliable. The reading does not ask you to substitute a display of momentum for the next piece of work still requiring attention.
glossary.hexagram.36.short: Fire within earth suggests clarity that cannot be expressed openly in the present setting.
glossary.hexagram.36.long: Fire within earth suggests clarity that cannot be expressed openly in the present setting. Protecting judgment differs from accepting an unlimited burden. Reduce unproductive public argument, preserve a reliable account and seek a suitable channel for support. The emphasis is on keeping what you know usable while conditions constrain its expression, rather than making concealment a permanent rule.
glossary.hexagram.37.short: Wind arising from fire places influence within a shared daily arrangement.
glossary.hexagram.37.long: Wind arising from fire places influence within a shared daily arrangement. Roles need clear expression and repeated follow-through, without being assigned by gender. State who maintains each ordinary task and ask when the distribution needs changing. A dependable household or group can preserve coordination while allowing the people in it to develop different needs over time.
glossary.hexagram.38.short: Fire and lake suggest different directions of movement.
glossary.hexagram.38.long: Fire and lake suggest different directions of movement. Opposition need not prevent cooperation on a limited task. Choose a small matter both participants recognize, rather than requiring complete agreement first. A difference of outlook is one part of the relationship; testing a modest shared action can provide information that an argument about the whole relationship cannot.
glossary.hexagram.39.short: Water above the mountain presents difficulty ahead of an already constrained route.
glossary.hexagram.39.long: Water above the mountain presents difficulty ahead of an already constrained route. A useful response may be returning to support, asking for guidance or choosing another path. Identify who can supply the missing information and compare the requirements of a detour. Pressing directly against the same obstruction is only one possible action, not a measure of commitment.
glossary.hexagram.40.short: Thunder above water suggests release as an active movement out of difficulty.
glossary.hexagram.40.long: Thunder above water suggests release as an active movement out of difficulty. Once pressure eases, attend to the remaining knot rather than starting another contest. Remove an obsolete requirement or finish the conversation that still restricts coordination. The aim is to let newly available room become useful, without assuming that relief means every practical issue has already resolved itself.
glossary.hexagram.41.short: The mountain above the lake directs attention to a reduction that changes the balance of an arrangement.
glossary.hexagram.41.long: The mountain above the lake directs attention to a reduction that changes the balance of an arrangement. Giving something up is useful when the purpose and limit are clear. Identify what can be reduced without removing essential support. Then check whether the decrease helps the whole task, rather than treating self-denial as valuable regardless of its effect.
glossary.hexagram.42.short: Wind above thunder presents an increase that can assist movement.
glossary.hexagram.42.long: Wind above thunder presents an increase that can assist movement. Added support matters through the improvement it enables, not only through the amount received. Use an offer to complete a task previously missing a condition, and explain how the assistance was used. This makes an increase accountable and helps others decide whether the support can continue.
glossary.hexagram.43.short: The lake above heaven accompanies a decisive disclosure or separation.
glossary.hexagram.43.long: The lake above heaven accompanies a decisive disclosure or separation. Clarity should not become a reason to escalate force. State the facts and the behaviour that needs changing, then define the boundary you will maintain. A firm decision can remain proportionate and understandable without requiring the other person to be defeated or humiliated.
glossary.hexagram.44.short: Wind beneath heaven suggests an influence encountered unexpectedly.
glossary.hexagram.44.long: Wind beneath heaven suggests an influence encountered unexpectedly. An interesting arrival is not yet a reliable connection. Establish a limited scope for the first exchange and notice how the other participant responds to a clear boundary. This lets an encounter provide information without giving it control over the wider arrangement before its effect is understood.
glossary.hexagram.45.short: The lake above earth gathers capacity into one place.
glossary.hexagram.45.long: The lake above earth gathers capacity into one place. Bringing people together still requires a reason to meet and a usable way to participate. Explain the common task, the coordination role and the point of entry for newcomers. The value of a gathering lies in connecting available resources and responses, rather than in counting attendance alone.
glossary.hexagram.46.short: Wood growing within earth presents gradual advancement through suitable conditions.
glossary.hexagram.46.long: Wood growing within earth presents gradual advancement through suitable conditions. This differs from forcing a single leap. Identify the practice and support needed for the next stage, then extend the scope after that stage becomes usable. Repeated preparation gives progress a footing and helps you distinguish a sustainable step from movement driven mainly by impatience.
glossary.hexagram.47.short: The lake without accessible water presents capacity that is difficult to use.
glossary.hexagram.47.long: The lake without accessible water presents capacity that is difficult to use. Constraint need not erase a reliable way of acting. Repeated explanation may have less value than naming one practical need and finding help with it. Reduce an effort that currently supplies no useful response, while preserving the resource or connection that can support a smaller next step.
glossary.hexagram.48.short: Water above wood gives the image of a well whose usefulness depends on access and maintenance.
glossary.hexagram.48.long: Water above wood gives the image of a well whose usefulness depends on access and maintenance. A resource can exist without reaching the person who needs it. Inspect the tool, the entry point and the responsibility for upkeep. Repair a leak or handover problem so that a stable source becomes usable rather than merely recognized as present.
glossary.hexagram.49.short: Fire within the lake frames a change in an arrangement whose parts no longer fit.
glossary.hexagram.49.long: Fire within the lake frames a change in an arrangement whose parts no longer fit. Trust develops through a clear reason and actions people can assess. Check the timing, the participants and the means of carrying the change forward. Announcing a transformation is different from establishing its replacement, so prepare the handover as carefully as the proposal.
glossary.hexagram.50.short: Fire above wood presents the transformation of ingredients through a vessel.
glossary.hexagram.50.long: Fire above wood presents the transformation of ingredients through a vessel. Good material still needs a sound means of preparation and delivery. Check the tool, the division of work and the handover before increasing output. The reading asks how capacity becomes nourishment or a usable result, rather than treating possession of ingredients as equivalent to a completed contribution.
glossary.hexagram.51.short: Repeated thunder emphasizes the response to a sudden disturbance.
glossary.hexagram.51.long: Repeated thunder emphasizes the response to a sudden disturbance. It does not forecast an accident. Confirm what has actually changed and which responsibility remains central before reorganizing everything. A startled response can settle into clear action when you attend to the immediate situation, rather than allowing the possibility of further disturbance to determine every choice.
glossary.hexagram.52.short: Repeated mountain emphasizes stopping at an appropriate boundary.
glossary.hexagram.52.long: Repeated mountain emphasizes stopping at an appropriate boundary. Stillness concerns an action and its limit, rather than suppressing every feeling or withdrawing from life. Pause a round of unproductive response and identify what belongs within your responsibility. Then decide what condition would make renewed engagement useful, so that a stop remains purposeful instead of becoming an indefinite barrier.
glossary.hexagram.53.short: Wood above the mountain suggests development through progressively secure footing.
glossary.hexagram.53.long: Wood above the mountain suggests development through progressively secure footing. Each stage needs a place to settle before the next can be sustained. Complete a necessary contact or agreement instead of skipping it to display progress. This gives a relationship or task time to become dependable without treating a slower pace as evidence that development has ceased.
glossary.hexagram.54.short: Thunder above the lake raises a question about unequal position or incomplete terms of participation.
glossary.hexagram.54.long: Thunder above the lake raises a question about unequal position or incomplete terms of participation. Historical relationship roles need not be imposed on a modern person. Ask who may decide what and whether each participant has freely agreed. A ceremony or an enthusiastic exchange cannot replace clear conditions about the responsibilities and choices people actually have.
glossary.hexagram.55.short: Thunder and lightning together suggest an abundance of activity and visibility.
glossary.hexagram.55.long: Thunder and lightning together suggest an abundance of activity and visibility. A full moment still has limits and can contain obscured information. Organize responsibilities and channels for feedback while the situation is busy. Check what the intensity of events has made harder to see, rather than assuming that greater activity automatically brings greater understanding.
glossary.hexagram.56.short: Fire above the mountain presents a temporary position in an unfamiliar setting.
glossary.hexagram.56.long: Fire above the mountain presents a temporary position in an unfamiliar setting. Secure a place to work or rest and understand the local terms before assuming broad authority. Clarify ownership, rules and sources of support. A traveller’s useful contribution can be limited and respectful, allowing participation without pretending that every part of the environment is already familiar.
glossary.hexagram.57.short: Repeated wind suggests influence through gradual, continuing entry.
glossary.hexagram.57.long: Repeated wind suggests influence through gradual, continuing entry. A gentle approach still needs a direction; repeated compliance without one can make the response difficult to understand. State a stable intention and express it through small actions over time. Where accommodation is needed, preserve the central boundary so that flexibility does not remove your practical means of participating.
glossary.hexagram.58.short: Repeated lake emphasizes pleasure in exchange that rests on sincerity.
glossary.hexagram.58.long: Repeated lake emphasizes pleasure in exchange that rests on sincerity. Maintaining a pleasant atmosphere is different from satisfying every request. Listen to the need being expressed and clarify what you are willing to offer. An honest boundary can preserve the quality of a conversation better than agreement given only to avoid a moment of disappointment.
glossary.hexagram.59.short: Wind over water suggests dispersion that calls for a point of reconnection.
glossary.hexagram.59.long: Wind over water suggests dispersion that calls for a point of reconnection. Breaking an arrangement apart is useful only when the purpose is clear. Find a reliable foothold and reopen one channel of response, then gather resources around a specific shared need. This helps release an unproductive division without creating another form of scattered effort.
glossary.hexagram.60.short: Water above the lake gives an image of capacity with a boundary.
glossary.hexagram.60.long: Water above the lake gives an image of capacity with a boundary. A limit should protect use without making participation needlessly harsh. Distinguish basic needs from commitments that can be adjusted, and explain why the rule exists. If the restriction consumes more effort than it saves, revise it rather than treating endurance of discomfort as proof that the rule is sound.
glossary.hexagram.61.short: Wind above the lake emphasizes an influence grounded in inner consistency.
glossary.hexagram.61.long: Wind above the lake emphasizes an influence grounded in inner consistency. Trust grows when a stated intention is matched by action. Connect a promise with one concrete delivery and notice whether the other participant responds willingly. Sincerity does not require setting aside evidence; a reliable exchange can remain open to information that changes the original expectation.
glossary.hexagram.62.short: Thunder above the mountain frames a limited excess in small matters while larger movement remains constrained.
glossary.hexagram.62.long: Thunder above the mountain frames a limited excess in small matters while larger movement remains constrained. The bird image directs attention toward a reachable position rather than a high leap. Check a detail that affects the present task and complete what is accessible. Care should remain proportionate, so that extra attention does not turn into an endless series of checks.
glossary.hexagram.63.short: Water above fire presents parts brought into a workable relationship.
glossary.hexagram.63.long: Water above fire presents parts brought into a workable relationship. Completion still requires maintenance, because a settled arrangement can become less usable through neglect or continued pushing. Prepare the repair materials and a clear handover. Check what should now be kept steady instead of assuming that more movement is always an improvement on what has already been accomplished.
glossary.hexagram.64.short: Fire above water presents parts not yet brought into a settled relationship.
glossary.hexagram.64.long: Fire above water presents parts not yet brought into a settled relationship. The crossing needs preparation through its final step, rather than confidence based only on how far you have come. Check the remaining sequence and the means of support at the endpoint. Celebrate progress while recognizing which condition still has to be fulfilled for the passage to become complete.

glossary.iching.clarity.long: Notice what you can establish directly, then use the image to ask a better question rather than filling an information gap with certainty.
glossary.iching.coordination.long: Agree on contributions, access and a review point so that goodwill becomes a task people can actually carry together.
glossary.iching.pacing.short: Choose a step your capacity can support
glossary.iching.pacing.long: Keep room to rest, seek help and change the plan as you learn, instead of making momentum the measure of progress.
glossary.pattern.yod.short: Two sextile-linked planets both form quincunxes to a third planet.
glossary.pattern.yod.long: A Yod combines one sextile with two quincunxes. It describes a relationship among three planetary themes that may call for repeated adjustment. Read it with the placements and actual experience; it does not confer a special identity or a fixed life mission.
glossary.pattern.zi_fu_chao_yuan.short: Zi Wei and Tian Fu meet across the life, wealth, career and travel areas.
glossary.pattern.zi_fu_chao_yuan.long: Zi Fu Chao Yuan names a traditional configuration involving Zi Wei and Tian Fu across the life, wealth, career and travel areas. It invites reflection on coordinating direction and maintaining resources, supplementing individual placements without independently predicting an achievement or event.
glossary.pattern.fu_xiang_chao_yuan.shor: Tian Fu and Tian Xiang meet across the life, wealth, career and travel areas.
glossary.pattern.fu_xiang_chao_yuan.long: Fu Xiang Chao Yuan names a traditional configuration involving Tian Fu and Tian Xiang across the life, wealth, career and travel areas. It invites reflection on maintaining resources and coordinating procedures. Read it with the whole chart and practical conditions rather than treating it as an independent prediction.
glossary.qimen.flag.kong_wang.short: A palace associated with branches absent from the current ten-pair group
glossary.qimen.flag.kong_wang.long: Void identifies a palace associated with branches absent from the current ten-pair group. It modifies an indicator in the nine-palace model and is read with gates, stars, palace relationships, and the actual question. It does not establish a particular event.

glossary.qimen.flag.men_po.long: Gate Pressure identifies a gate element restraining its palace element. It modifies an indicator in the nine-palace model and is read with gates, stars, palace relationships, and the actual question. It does not establish a particular event.

glossary.qimen.flag.wu_bu_yu_shi.long: Hour Mismatch identifies a traditional restraining relation between hour and day stems. It modifies an indicator in the nine-palace model and is read with gates, stars, palace relationships, and the actual question. It does not establish a particular event.
glossary.tarot.action.short: A small step you can actually try.
glossary.tarot.action.long: Action means turning attention into a small, observable step. Check the time and resources it needs, try it, and use actual feedback to adjust the next step rather than treating a card as a decision maker.
glossary.tarot.reflection.short: Time to distinguish an observation from your interpretation.
glossary.tarot.reflection.long: Reflection creates space between an observation, its interpretation, and the feelings that follow. Write down a specific example and consider other explanations before treating a first impression as a fact.
glossary.tarot.communication.short: Sharing a clear question and listening to a direct response.
glossary.tarot.communication.long: Communication combines expressing a need with listening to the response. Begin with a concrete question, check that both people understand it similarly, and discuss an arrangement each person is willing to try.
glossary.tarot.boundaries.short: The scope you are comfortable offering or accepting.
glossary.tarot.boundaries.long: Boundaries describe what a person is comfortable offering, accepting, or taking responsibility for. Clarify time, energy, and responsibilities, and leave room to renegotiate when circumstances change.
glossary.tarot.review.short: Looking back at a plan with information gained afterwards.
glossary.tarot.review.long: Review means revisiting a choice with information gained afterwards. Separate the original expectation, the actual result, and a step to adjust next time; the purpose is learning from experience rather than judging personal worth.
glossary.tarot.preparation.short: Checking the time and resources a step needs.
glossary.tarot.preparation.long: Preparation means checking the time, information, and resources a step requires. List what is already available and what still needs attention, then complete one small check to make the next step concrete.
glossary.tarot.cooperation.short: Shared work supported by clear roles and mutual response.
glossary.tarot.cooperation.long: Cooperation supports shared work through clear roles and mutual response. Agree on responsibilities, a time to communicate, and a way to revise the arrangement so that a shared goal becomes understandable action.
glossary.tarot.choice.short: A next step considered in light of needs and known conditions.
glossary.tarot.choice.long: Choice means comparing feasible next steps against current needs and known conditions. Note the resources each option requires and how easily it can be revised, leaving room to gather more information when needed.
glossary.tarot.feelings.short: The emotional experience and comfort you notice in a situation.
glossary.tarot.feelings.long: Feelings are the emotions, comfort, and subjective experience noticed in a situation. Describe the experience first, then distinguish it from assumptions about another person’s motives to leave room for expression and understanding.
glossary.wands_01.short: give a fresh impulse a practical first step
glossary.wands_01.long: The sprouting wand suggests a new impulse before there is a finished plan. It differs from the Magician’s coordination of skills already available. Inspiration becomes usable through a first attempt. If energy is low, reduce the scale; if ideas are competing, choose one and identify the materials and time needed to see how it behaves in practice.
glossary.wands_02.short: look beyond your current routine and compare possibilities
glossary.wands_02.long: The globe and distant view make planning and possible directions central. Conflict is not the card’s only or defining subject. Unlike the Three of Wands, this scene precedes a wider commitment. Compare two options using their preparation requirements and available reach. If the comparison keeps expanding, choose a reversible experiment that provides information the planning stage cannot supply.
glossary.wands_03.short: prepare for responses to work already set in motion
glossary.wands_03.long: The figure looking toward the ships suggests that an initiative has already moved beyond the planning stage. Attention turns to outside responses and what can be received next. Unlike the Two of Wands’ comparison of possibilities, this card asks how you follow through. If replies are slow, check the handover and expected timetable before deciding the effort has failed.
glossary.wands_04.short: make space for a shared milestone
glossary.wands_04.long: The garland and celebration emphasize a shared milestone and a place to gather. This is not a prediction about relationship status. Unlike the World’s completed cycle, a milestone can be acknowledged while further work remains. Ask what made the occasion possible and who needs inclusion. If the celebration feels strained, adjust the arrangement instead of requiring everyone to display the same mood.
glossary.wands_05.short: use disagreement to discover what needs coordination
glossary.wands_05.long: The raised wands point in competing directions, making friction and uncoordinated effort visible. Disagreement may concern practice or methods rather than hostility. Unlike the Five of Swords’ cost of winning, the useful question is how a contest becomes constructive. Agree on what is being tested. If opinions have been suppressed, invite one specific requirement from each participant before deciding.
glossary.wands_06.short: receive recognition and acknowledge the effort behind it
glossary.wands_06.long: The rider’s wreath and surrounding people connect achievement with public acknowledgment. Recognition is a response to visible work, not a promise of continued success. Identify what was actually completed and who contributed to it. If approval has become the only measure that matters, compare the feedback with the result and decide which standard you want to carry into the next task.
glossary.wands_07.short: stand behind a priority you have chosen
glossary.wands_07.long: The figure holds higher ground while meeting pressure from below. The theme is defending a position already taken, rather than joining every contest. Unlike the Five of Wands, not every disagreement here deserves equal attention. Choose the boundary that matters most. If constant defence is exhausting, reduce the number of arguments you enter and state what remains open to negotiation.
glossary.wands_08.short: organise a burst of movement or information
glossary.wands_08.long: The moving wands emphasize pace, messages and transitions already underway. The absence of a visible person does not remove the need for coordination. Unlike the Chariot’s steering, this card asks how you handle several developments arriving close together. Confirm what has been received and what needs a reply. If movement stalls, inspect the sequence before adding another urgent message.
glossary.wands_09.short: protect what you have built while recognising fatigue
glossary.wands_09.long: The guarded figure brings experience and fatigue to the boundary. Persistence has a history here, unlike the Seven of Wands’ more immediate defence. Past difficulty can inform preparation without making every new request a threat. Identify the condition that actually needs checking. If vigilance has become constant, schedule a handover or rest interval rather than asking yourself to remain alert indefinitely.
glossary.wands_10.short: redistribute a load that has become difficult to carry
glossary.wands_10.long: The bundle obstructs the carrier’s view, showing how accumulated responsibility can impair movement. The issue is load, not a test of personal worth. Compared with the Nine of Wands’ guarded persistence, this card calls for redistribution. Identify a task that can be delegated or ended. Releasing it requires a named handover, rather than silently dropping work someone else depends on.
glossary.wands_page.short: approach a new interest with a learner's curiosity
glossary.wands_page.long: The Page studies the wand as an object of curiosity. This is a role of exploration, not an age or gender assignment. Unlike the Knight’s active pursuit, the Page can remain open while learning what an idea requires. If enthusiasm spreads across too many beginnings, choose one question to test and record what makes you want to return to it.
glossary.wands_knight.short: bring energy to a bounded experiment
glossary.wands_knight.long: The moving horse puts enthusiasm into motion. This can describe a style of action rather than a particular person arriving in your life. Compared with the Page’s exploration, the Knight has begun the pursuit. Check what sustains effort after the exciting start. If pace keeps swinging, separate departure, progress and handover, and commit only to the stage you can carry.
glossary.wands_queen.short: encourage expression through warmth and confidence
glossary.wands_queen.long: The sunflower and black cat bring visible warmth together with independence. This role is not reserved for a particular gender. The Queen encourages participation through confidence rather than directing every response. If you feel obliged to maintain the group’s energy, make room for your own quieter needs. Inviting someone to contribute works best when they can bring a different style.
glossary.wands_king.short: give a shared project a clear direction
glossary.wands_king.long: The King’s held wand and outward attention connect vision with the ability to guide sustained effort. Unlike the Knight’s personal momentum, this role involves other people’s participation. State the destination and ask what resources the work needs. If conviction has begun to overpower feedback, invite a specific objection before settling the method; leadership includes listening to the people carrying it out.
glossary.cups_01.short: welcome a fresh feeling without demanding an immediate label
glossary.cups_01.long: The overflowing cup suggests an opening for feeling, care or creativity. It does not establish that a new relationship will begin. Unlike the Two of Cups, a reciprocal exchange has not yet been shown. Give an emerging feeling room without demanding a response from someone else. If expression feels difficult, share one manageable need rather than the entire emotional story.
glossary.cups_02.long: The facing figures make reciprocity central. Each person brings a cup; connection depends on both responses rather than one person’s intention. Unlike the Lovers’ wider question of values and choice, this scene focuses on an exchange. If pace or effort differs, ask about contact and boundaries directly. The card cannot establish another person’s commitment without their actual participation.
glossary.cups_03.short: enjoy encouragement within a supportive group
glossary.cups_03.long: The three raised cups emphasize friendship, celebration and a network of support. The number of figures is not evidence of an affair or hidden rival. Unlike the Ten of Cups’ sustained sense of belonging, this scene centres on gathering. If social involvement has become draining, choose a smaller meeting or name the interaction that needs a clearer boundary.
glossary.cups_04.short: pause long enough to understand your lack of interest
glossary.cups_04.long: The seated figure has not taken the offered cup. The scene leaves room for rest, disinterest and an opportunity that has not been noticed; it does not establish ingratitude. Unlike the Five of Cups, the emphasis is not a named loss. If you are ready to re-engage, respond to one suitable invitation and check whether you want novelty or recovery.
glossary.cups_05.short: acknowledge disappointment without losing sight of remaining support
glossary.cups_05.long: The fallen cups make disappointment visible, while the standing pair remains available behind the figure. Existing support does not cancel a real loss. Compared with the Three of Swords’ sharper hurt, this card asks where attention rests afterwards. If you are beginning to turn toward what remains, accept one offer of help without requiring yourself to stop feeling sad first.
glossary.cups_06.short: draw comfort from a familiar and generous memory
glossary.cups_06.long: The flower-filled cups connect kindness with familiarity and memory. They do not forecast someone from the past returning. Unlike the Three of Cups’ current gathering, this card asks how earlier experiences shape an exchange. Keep what is comforting, while comparing remembered impressions with present behaviour. A meaningful memory can inform your response without deciding what another person is like now.
glossary.cups_07.short: sort attractive possibilities by what can actually be tried
glossary.cups_07.long: The varied images in the cups make possibility and projection visible at the same time. An appealing picture is not yet a workable option. Unlike the Two of Wands’ more grounded planning, this scene asks which imagined choice has supporting information. Compare one attractive possibility with its actual requirements, and remove an option that depends entirely on assumptions you cannot check.
glossary.cups_08.short: move away from a pattern that no longer meets your needs
glossary.cups_08.long: The departing figure leaves an arrangement that once held value. Moving on does not require declaring the whole past worthless. Unlike a broader transition, this card emphasizes a deliberate search for something the current situation no longer supplies. If leaving and returning keep alternating, name the unmet need and compare what would change through adjustment or through departure.
glossary.cups_09.short: enjoy a satisfaction you have helped create
glossary.cups_09.long: The arranged cups frame satisfaction as a personal experience. An encouraging image does not establish that every wish will be fulfilled. Unlike the Ten of Cups’ shared belonging, this scene asks what feels sufficient to you. If visible accomplishments still leave an unmet need, distinguish enjoyment you actually experience from possessions or appearances maintained mainly for other people’s approval.
glossary.cups_10.short: nurture a sense of belonging people can share
glossary.cups_10.long: The figures beneath the rainbow emphasize belonging that can be shared. The image does not prescribe a family structure or a relationship status. Unlike the Nine of Cups’ personal satisfaction, this scene depends on mutual participation. If the ideal picture does not match daily life, ask how each person experiences support and space instead of requiring one appearance of happiness.
glossary.cups_page.short: express a new feeling in a gentle and exploratory way
glossary.cups_page.long: The unexpected fish makes a new emotional or creative response visible. A first expression can be sincere without being fully formed. The Page describes a learning role rather than someone’s age. If imagination begins supplying more than the facts support, write down the observation separately from the hope it prompted, then use a gentle question to clarify the difference.
glossary.cups_knight.short: offer warmth with a clear and considerate invitation
glossary.cups_knight.long: The offered cup turns feeling into an invitation. Compared with the Knight of Wands’ pursuit of action, this role asks how an emotional intention reaches another person. A warm message needs room for a voluntary response and a practical arrangement. If appealing words are not followed through, clarify the date, available effort and scope before relying on the invitation.
glossary.cups_queen.short: listen with care while keeping room for your own feelings
glossary.cups_queen.long: The Queen’s attention to the cup suggests careful listening to emotional experience. This role can be practised by anyone. Understanding another person’s feeling does not make you responsible for managing all of it. If care has become absorbing, ask whether they want listening or practical assistance, and state the amount of support you are actually able to offer.
glossary.cups_king.short: respond steadily without dismissing complicated feelings
glossary.cups_king.long: The King remains seated while the water moves around him. Emotional steadiness means responding with awareness, not concealing every feeling. Compared with the Queen’s receptive attention, this role also involves coordinating an exchange. If suppressed emotion or a changing mood is shaping the discussion, name the feeling and choose a time when you can address the actual issue clearly.
glossary.swords_01.short: cut through confusion with a precise question
glossary.swords_01.long: The upright sword gives an idea a clear edge. Clarity can open a problem, but a sharp statement is not automatically a sound conclusion. Unlike the King of Swords’ established judgment, this is a starting point. If the idea remains confused, formulate one answerable question and identify the information that would let you decide whether the distinction is useful.
glossary.swords_02.short: give two competing needs an honest hearing
glossary.swords_02.long: The blindfold and crossed swords show a balance maintained while some information stays outside the decision. This differs from the Seven of Cups’ attraction to many imagined options. Ask which fact you have avoided or cannot yet obtain. If the stalemate is loosening, compare the consequences of the two choices rather than waiting for an option with no cost at all.
glossary.swords_03.short: acknowledge hurt and make your needs understandable
glossary.swords_03.long: The pierced heart and rain make hurt explicit. The image can reflect a painful conversation or separation without establishing betrayal. Unlike the Five of Cups’ attention to what remains after disappointment, this scene asks you to acknowledge the wound itself. If expression is becoming possible, share one need with someone able to listen, without forcing a complete explanation at once.
glossary.swords_04.short: take a defined interval away from demands
glossary.swords_04.long: The resting posture and still swords emphasize a pause in active response. This is a reflection on recovery and attention, not a diagnosis. Unlike the Hanged Man’s deliberate change of perspective, the Four of Swords asks what rest makes possible. If stopping feels difficult or the pause has lost its boundary, agree when you will review the task again.
glossary.swords_05.short: consider the cost of winning an unhelpful argument
glossary.swords_05.long: The held swords and departing figures place winning beside the cost of an encounter. The picture does not establish anyone’s character. Unlike the Five of Wands’ contest over methods, this card asks whether continuing the argument serves the relationship or task. If you want to end the confrontation, name one behaviour you will stop and one condition for reopening discussion.
glossary.swords_06.short: use a transition to create a more workable setting
glossary.swords_06.long: The boat carries both people and swords into a quieter setting. A transition may reduce disturbance while some unresolved concerns travel with it. This does not predict a journey. Unlike the Eight of Cups’ search for meaning, the emphasis is on a workable passage. If change stalls, clarify the support and handover needed rather than assuming a new setting will solve everything.
glossary.swords_07.short: choose a strategy with clear information boundaries
glossary.swords_07.long: The figure carries some swords while others remain behind. Strategy, incomplete disclosure and an unfinished task are all possible questions; the image is not evidence of theft. Distinguish information you may reasonably keep private from facts another person needs for a shared decision. If clarification is overdue, disclose the relevant detail without abandoning every personal boundary in the process.
glossary.swords_08.short: separate a feeling of restriction into changeable conditions
glossary.swords_08.long: The blindfold and bindings make restriction visible, while the surrounding space invites closer inspection. Some limits may be external and real; the card does not declare them imaginary. If room to choose is returning, distinguish a fixed constraint from missing information and from an action you have not tried. Change one accessible condition before expecting the entire situation to open.
glossary.swords_09.short: bring repetitive worry back to what you can handle now
glossary.swords_09.long: The waking figure makes repetitive worry visible rather than forecasting a disaster or diagnosing a condition. Unlike the Eight of Swords’ restriction, this card asks how a concern keeps returning in thought. Write down the question that appears most often and identify what can be checked now. If support is needed, bring that specific concern to someone you trust.
glossary.swords_10.short: recognise when a method has reached its limit
glossary.swords_10.long: The many swords depict an approach pushed beyond usefulness, while the distant light leaves space after its ending. This is not a prediction about physical events. Unlike the Tower’s abrupt exposure of a weak structure, the emphasis is on stopping further depletion. If recovery has begun, remove one ineffective demand and arrange the basic support needed before taking on a replacement.
glossary.swords_page.short: gather information through alert and respectful questions
glossary.swords_page.long: The Page holds the sword while attending to a changing setting. Curiosity and alertness precede a settled judgment. Unlike the Knight’s rapid response, this role can remain in the information-gathering stage. If a conclusion has come too quickly, check the source, date and context of the message. A perceptive question is more useful than claiming the whole picture is already clear.
glossary.swords_knight.short: act on a clear idea without losing the wider picture
glossary.swords_knight.long: The moving horse and forward posture show thought turning quickly into action. Speed can help address a clear problem while also leaving background unheard. If urgency has overtaken understanding, restate the other person’s actual claim before challenging it. Choose one checkable disagreement and allow time for new information, rather than making a forceful delivery the measure of a sound argument.
glossary.swords_queen.short: state a boundary clearly while listening fairly
glossary.swords_queen.long: The upright sword and extended hand combine a boundary with an invitation to speak. Clear discernment need not mean emotional coldness, and the role is not assigned by gender. If defensiveness has sharpened the exchange, separate the observed fact, your response to it and the request you want to make. Directness can remain fair without becoming a verdict about the person.
glossary.swords_king.short: use consistent standards to organise a difficult question
glossary.swords_king.long: The seated posture and controlled sword suggest judgment applied through a stable standard. Authority becomes useful when its reasoning can be examined. Unlike the Ace of Swords’ new distinction, this role concerns an established decision process. If the standard constrains others while exempting you, test it on a comparable case and invite someone to identify the information you have overlooked.
glossary.pentacles_01.short: give a practical opportunity a stable starting place
glossary.pentacles_01.long: The coin and garden entrance suggest an opportunity with practical requirements. This does not promise an increase in wealth. Unlike the Ten of Pentacles’ established continuity, the Ace concerns a beginning that needs material support. If an offer remains vague, check the time, tools and responsible person before treating it as available, then complete one piece of preparation you can control.
glossary.pentacles_02.short: adjust a workable rhythm among competing tasks
glossary.pentacles_02.long: The linked coins move while the ships meet changing waves. Balance is an ongoing adjustment of time and resources, not proof that every commitment can be maintained. Unlike the Four of Pentacles’ holding pattern, this card asks how priorities rotate. If coordination is slipping, pause one lower-priority task and distinguish a fixed responsibility from an arrangement that can be renegotiated.
glossary.pentacles_03.short: combine different skills around an agreed standard
glossary.pentacles_03.long: The craftsperson and discussion around the structure connect skill with a shared standard. Being busy is different from coordinating expertise. Ask who supplies the design, who carries out the work and who checks the result. If collaboration is misaligned, review one sample together. A clear division of roles can respect different contributions without ranking the people making them.
glossary.pentacles_04.short: protect resources without closing every opening
glossary.pentacles_04.long: The coins are held close across the figure’s body. Retention can protect stability while also reducing room for exchange. Unlike the Two of Pentacles’ flexible rotation, this scene asks what is being secured. If you want to loosen control, release a manageable amount first. If resources are being relinquished too quickly, check basic needs before calling every act of holding on a problem.
glossary.pentacles_05.short: look for accessible support when resources feel scarce
glossary.pentacles_05.long: The lit window and figures outside make need and access to support visible together. This is not a prediction of poverty or a physical condition. Ask which resource is lacking and whether an available service or trusted person can help. If assistance is becoming accessible, clarify how to request it; feeling excluded does not establish that every door is closed.
glossary.pentacles_06.short: make giving and receiving clear and proportionate
glossary.pentacles_06.long: The scales beside the distributed coins connect generosity with the power to set terms. Giving is useful when the arrangement is clear to both sides. Ask what is offered, what is expected in return and who may change the terms. If support has become conditional in an uncomfortable way, clarify that condition before accepting rather than assuming gratitude requires agreement to everything.
glossary.pentacles_07.short: review gradual progress before adding more effort
glossary.pentacles_07.long: The pause beside growing pentacles suggests evaluation after sustained effort. Waiting alone does not establish a return. Unlike the Eight of Pentacles’ active practice, this card asks whether the current approach still merits your time. Set a review point and compare observable progress with the resources being used. Continuing, adjusting and stopping can each be reasonable responses to what you find.
glossary.pentacles_08.short: improve a skill through attentive repetition
glossary.pentacles_08.long: The repeated carving emphasizes learning through attentive work. Repetition is useful when it changes the quality of what you can do, rather than only increasing the count. Compared with the Seven of Pentacles’ assessment of a longer investment, this card focuses on the next practice cycle. Choose one detail to improve and ask for feedback precise enough to guide another attempt.
glossary.pentacles_09.short: enjoy the quality of life your steady work supports
glossary.pentacles_09.long: The garden, mature pentacles and trained bird connect independence with cultivated conditions. This is not a label for wealth or social status. Unlike the Ten of Pentacles’ shared continuity, the emphasis is on the quality of life you have shaped. If maintaining appearances has become costly in time or effort, retain the comfort you value and reduce what serves only display.
glossary.pentacles_10.short: care for shared resources that extend beyond one task
glossary.pentacles_10.long: The people, animals and established setting connect resources with continuity across a group. The image does not prescribe a family model. Unlike the Nine of Pentacles’ personal autonomy, this card asks how an arrangement survives beyond one person’s effort. If inherited expectations no longer fit, discuss use, maintenance and handover so that useful experience can remain while participation is renegotiated.
glossary.pentacles_page.short: approach a practical skill with careful curiosity
glossary.pentacles_page.long: The Page studies a tangible object, placing learning in contact with something that can be handled and checked. This is a practice role, not a prediction about qualifications. Unlike the Knight’s continuing routine, the Page is establishing foundations. If attention is scattered, choose one basic operation, prepare its materials and define what completion looks like before adding another learning plan.
glossary.pentacles_knight.short: maintain progress through reliable and measured effort
glossary.pentacles_knight.long: The stationary horse and held pentacle emphasize preparation and dependable execution. A measured pace is different from doing nothing. Compared with the Knight of Wands’ energetic pursuit, this role concerns showing up repeatedly with what the task needs. If the routine has become mechanical, remove an obsolete check or update a step while preserving the reliability that makes the work usable.
glossary.pentacles_queen.short: offer practical care that includes your own needs
glossary.pentacles_queen.long: The Queen’s attention to the pentacle and living surroundings connects care with practical conditions. Anyone can occupy this role; it does not require unlimited availability. Unlike purely emotional support, the focus is on making daily life workable. If maintenance has consumed your own space, distinguish essential care from additional demands and invite the people benefiting from the arrangement to share its upkeep.
glossary.pentacles_king.short: manage practical resources in a dependable way
glossary.pentacles_king.long: The stable seat and abundant setting emphasize resources managed over time. Reliability comes through maintenance rather than possession alone. Compared with the Emperor’s establishment of a framework, this role asks how well that framework now serves people. If comfortable routines or control have displaced usefulness, check who can actually access the resources and make the conditions of sharing and handover clear.
glossary.vedic.sidereal_zodiac.short: A zodiac referenced through a sidereal offset
glossary.vedic.sidereal_zodiac.long: Vedic positions subtract an ayanamsa from tropical longitude. The reference differs from the Western tropical zodiac, so the labels should not be mixed directly.
glossary.vedic.ayanamsa.short: Angular offset between tropical and sidereal reference points
glossary.vedic.ayanamsa.long: The project uses Lahiri ayanamsa to convert shared ephemeris positions to sidereal longitude. The value is an angle in degrees, not an additional fortune score.
glossary.vedic.bhava.short: A life-area division in a Vedic chart
glossary.vedic.bhava.long: This project uses Whole Sign houses in its Vedic chart. The rising sign forms the first house and subsequent signs form the remaining houses; unknown-time charts omit them.
glossary.vedic.vimshottari.pinyin: bǎi èr shí nián zhōu qī
glossary.vedic.vimshottari.short: A planetary period sequence starting from the Moon’s lunar sector
glossary.vedic.vimshottari.long: The birth Moon’s sector selects the first period lord, and progress through that sector determines the remaining first-period length. The full 120-year sequence is a traditional timing framework rather than a measure of lifespan.
glossary.vedic.d1.long: D1 is the base chart of sidereal sign positions, with houses set by the rising sign and Whole Sign rules. It provides a different layer of observation from D9.
glossary.vedic.d9.short: A divisional chart with nine parts per sign
glossary.vedic.d9.long: D9 is the chart designation for Navamsa, with each division spanning 3°20′. It is traditionally used to reflect on relationships and inner strengths; a precise rising point is not invented for an unknown birth time.
glossary.vedic.retrograde.short: Negative apparent longitude speed as seen from Earth
glossary.vedic.retrograde.long: Retrograde is an apparent-motion classification, recorded separately from combustion and dignity. It is neither physical backward travel nor a prediction of a difficult event.
